beforeCard.prompt: Как называется переход снега или льда прямо в водяной пар?

answers.note: Кальвинг — отделение глыб льда от фронта ледника или шельфа.
Сублимация переводит лёд непосредственно в водяной пар без жидкой стадии.
Фирнизация превращает многолетний снег в зернистый фирн, а затем в ледниковый лёд.
Абляция — совокупная потеря массы ледником из-за таяния, испарения и откалывания.

beforeCard.explanation: Это сублимация. Процесс удаляет массу с ледяной поверхности без образования талой воды.

literal.prompt: Как называется переход снега или льда прямо в водяной пар?

finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: NSIDC says sublimation in very dry Antarctica can make glaciers disappear and defines it as solids transitioning directly to gas. The other choices name different glacier processes: calving breaks off ice chunks; firn forms from compressed snow; ablation is a seasonal mass-loss process. Only sublimation matches ice/snow directly becoming vapor.
finalGroupBindings.locator: NSIDC Science of Glaciers L67,L72,L84,L108; Science of Ice Shelves L75

finalGroupBindings.literal: Это сублимация. Процесс удаляет массу с ледяной поверхности без образования талой воды.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: NSIDC L67 says solids transition directly to gas and that Antarctic glaciers can disappear because of sublimation. The explanation’s no-liquid inference follows from that phase definition; it does not claim that all polar ice loss occurs this way.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Кальвинг — отделение глыб льда от фронта ледника или шельфа.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: This literal is the calving distractor, not sublimation. NSIDC says ice shelves periodically calve (break off) chunks at the seaward edge, producing icebergs; it also documents tidewater-glacier calving. The note accurately teaches solid-fragment detachment, distinct from a phase transition.
finalGroupBindings.locator: NSIDC Science of Ice Shelves L75,L77-L78; Science of Glaciers L155

finalGroupBindings.literal: В очень сухих районах Антарктиды сублимация может приводить к исчезновению ледников.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: This literal is the correct sublimation note. NSIDC explicitly says that in very dry parts of Antarctica glaciers can grow slowly or disappear because of sublimation, and defines it as solids transitioning directly to gas. The note adds that Antarctic glacier consequence beyond the prompt/key.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Фирнизация превращает многолетний снег в зернистый фирн, а затем в ледниковый лёд.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: NSIDC states that snow surviving one melt season forms denser compressed firn, and further compression of snow and firn builds glacier ice. The note accurately describes snow-to-firn-to-ice compaction, not a solid-to-vapor phase change.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Абляция — совокупная потеря массы ледником из-за таяния, испарения и откалывания.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: The note describes ablation as broad glacier mass loss involving melt, evaporation and calving. NSIDC describes glacier losses from melting, evaporation and calving, characterizes ablation as a natural seasonal part of glacier life, and locates most melting/evaporation in lower ablation areas. This supports it as a broad glacier-loss distractor, not the specific solid-to-vapor process.

authorAssessment.fullPrompt: Как называется переход снега или льда прямо в водяной пар?
authorAssessment.note: Кальвинг — отделение глыб льда от фронта ледника или шельфа.
authorAssessment.grammar: “Кальвинг” is a natural Russian name of a process in answer to “Как называется переход…?”; it is a glacier/ice process parallel in category but distinct in mechanism from the other choices.
authorAssessment.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: The whole variant is a credible distractor: calving removes ice from a glacier or ice-shelf front, and its note correctly says chunks detach. It is wrong because the prompt asks for a phase transition from solid snow/ice directly to vapor, while calving breaks off solid chunks that remain ice. The note usefully distinguishes a mass-loss mechanism from a phase change.

authorAssessment.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: This is the correct key: NSIDC explicitly defines sublimation as solids transitioning directly to gas, matching snow/ice to water vapor. The added note is about this same option and is true: in very dry parts of Antarctica, sublimation can make glaciers grow slowly or disappear. That consequence adds a concrete own-option fact beyond the prompt/key and explains why the process matters in polar glaciology.
